latin_text: Therefore an angel is not unity itself, or else he would be God, or there would be many gods, which cannot even be conceived. For what will be one if not unity? It is left for an angel to be a number.
english_translation: Therefore an angel is not unity itself, or else he would be God, or there would be many gods, which cannot even be conceived. For what will be one if not unity? It is left for an angel to be a number.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico's Kabbalistic definition: an angel is *not* unity itself (which would make it God); therefore, an angel *must be a number*—a multiplicity that participates in divine unity. [INFERRED] This integrates Pythagorean number theology with Kabbalistic Sefirotic doctrine: each Sefirah is a distinct number, distinct emanation, yet all participate in divine unity. Angels embody this principle: each angel is uniquely itself (a distinct number) while remaining ordered toward the absolute unity.

The philosophical function is to establish angelic ontology through participation: angels are multiplicities participating in unity, precisely because they are creatures (not God). This explains the ninefold hierarchy: nine distinct angelic choirs, each uniquely numbered, all ordered to the One.

[VERIFIED] The Oration (O.1.11) invokes the ladder of angelic being. Commento (C.1.3) describes angelic transformation. Being & Unity grounds it: participated being is precisely this—multiplicities receiving being from and ordered toward the divine unity.
notes: HARVESTER passage: H.TE3.C1.1 | Angel as number; angelic ontology based on participation in divine unity
